newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end lower after narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end lower after narrow trade.

text.p: Greek shares ended 0.43 percent lower in narrow trade after settling with mild gains on Tuesday. Three member firms not allowed to trade on Wednesday after non-compliance with settlement regulations.
Market watchers expected a subdued market this week.

"The market is preoccupied with settlement problems that need to be addressed. The clearing house must improve its operations to international standards. The every day occurrence of member brokers not allowed to trade is undermining the market," said analyst Tasos Rapakoulias at Katsoulis Securities.
He said fundamentals were good and investors with a long term outlook would be rewarded with strong returns after the current problems were resolved.
Greece is cutting the marker 12-month T-bill rate by 50 basis points down to 11.50 percent in December.
Last Friday, Italy's Concretum agreed to buy a 12 percent stake in Heracles Cements for 32.23 billion drachmas or 5,320 drachmas a share from National Bank. Heracles closed up 10 drachmas at 3,050.

The Athens general share index closed down 0.43 percent or 3.88 points lower at 908.08 from Tuesday's 911.96 close after opening at 912.42. Turnover jumped to 95.9 billion drachmas after a giant 25-million-share block trade in Heracles Cements.
